items.title: Conflicting evidence on triage time
items.whyItMatters: The controlled study found no change in triage time while the uncontrolled one found a halving (claim c3); the intake cannot assume the template will shorten its nine days.
items.opportunity: Measure lead time weekly before and after each countermeasure instead of predicting it.

items.title: No evaluation of this intake's combination
items.whyItMatters: The confirmed empty search found no study of a template introduced within a lean redesign of a central intake.
items.opportunity: Report the redesign so others can learn from it.

items.title: Practice workload and bypass are rarely measured
items.whyItMatters: Templates can move work into practices and 38 percent of referrals bypassed fields in one study (claims c2, c4).
items.opportunity: Track bypass (attached letters) and sample practice completion time as balancing measures.

items.title: Practices without rapid test kits
items.whyItMatters: Required test fields returned the most referrals from practices without rapid kits (claim c5), which may be rural or low-resource practices.
items.opportunity: Report returned referrals by practice group and allow a documented exception when a test is unavailable.

items.title: Rework inside the intake
items.whyItMatters: Most triage nurse time may be rework, which a template alone does not remove.
items.opportunity: Map the value stream first and remove intake-side waste before or alongside the template.

errorsFound: The need frames the template as the solution; the evidence supports it only for completeness, not for triage time.
reevaluation: The gaps favour a lean redesign that tests the template as one countermeasure, with triage time measured locally and practice workload as a balancing measure.
summary: Five gaps; the conflict on triage time and the unmeasured practice workload are high severity.
